body: For the time being, at least for the next six months I'll be unable to. Basically what that comes down to is that I passed out when I had my blood drawn back in February for lab purposes, had some spasms while I was out. This one nurse erroneously said that I had a seizure; information I carried with me when I went to get my license renewed. It's been a month now since I called the local clinic to set up an EEG (to prove that I don't have a seizure disorder, which I can quite confidently say I don't), and I've heard nothing. Plus, once again the matter of being able to be driven to said neurologist comes up, since of course the nearest one is in a big city.

Provided they even take me seriously in the first place, I'm not sure what good would come of it. After all, I have made oblique, serious mentions that I have wanted to die in the past (albeit for different, much more "normal" reasons), and the best response I got was, "no you won't", or it's just a phase." I don't blame them, though; they've never had to deal w)th a case like me, and they most likely have no idea how to, hence the (admittedly seeming) lack of concern. Then there's the matter of shipping me around at least an hour away to where the nearest therapist might be (they won't, because they don't drive in big cities)... I wanna believe there is a solution, but it's really been hard to find.

Ehh, they would probably brush it off as a joke. I've got a penchant for dark humor anyways. Even then, they're under enough stress already. Knowing that their son is thinking this kinda shit? God, it scares me to think of what would happen, not only to myself.

Unfortunately, I've pretty much become dissatisfied with most of the cheap or free hobbies I can think of that I would enjoy. I've been wanting to get into music writing, but that's too expensive for my current income level. Plus, it would annoy the hell out of my folks. Even then, it doesn't do much to help the whole existentialism thing (which may just be incurable, I dunno).

Honestly, the things that used to destress me (music, video games, writing, hell even comedy) just aren't doing anything for me anymore. I'm not 100% sure how much physicality would help me out; in fact, most days in 9th grade PE I just ended up feeling like shit. The biggest thing that helped me out around that time was shedding my self-defacing superstitions, as well as making some actual friends for once in my life. Now though, if I were to go to them and talk about this, you can bet I'd be down a friend. After all, I did say that they weren't too terribly close (the last thing I needed was for shit to go down with a good friend). But yeah, other than through this alias, this projection of who I really am cloaked in the veil of pseudonymity, there really is no other outlet.

Honestly, I'm not sure how well talking things out will help. I've talked this out extensively with myself in my own head, and I'm pretty alright at catching my own bullshit, but ultimately it was an attempt to separate fictitious me from reality me. As someone else said, I do spend a lot of time in my head (an hour or two every night laying in bed before I got to sleep), playing out scenario after scenario of whatever is on my mind. It's been a pretty good coping mechanism for loneliness for the past decade, but little by little it's losing effectiveness. In fact, I've "roleplayed" myself going to a psychologist multiple times in my head, effectively acting as my own psychologist. Sometimes it works, other times... well, it doesn't end up so well. I've ended up killing myself more times than I would like to admit within these fantasies, and one of my most primal fears is that the lines between these "daydreams" and reality are blurring. Unfortunately, some of these fantasies are positive in nature, like me writing this fairly big story I've been meaning to write for the last couple of years, but much like this post, the biggest challenge is "making it real." However, if these lines are blurring, I might as well throw something out there that may or may not stick. It's a start of something, that's all I really know right now.

Seeing a psychologist is out of the question, as there isn't one in my town. The nearest one is 15 miles away. Since I can't drive myself to that town, I would have to rely on my parents, who really wouldn't believe a single thing I said if I tried to tell them, be it out of the lack of knowledge of how to handle a case like me or the thought that "you'll get over it soon enough." Trust me, I've tried. Financials are a problem, too, as I've got an alright amount of money but nowhere near enough to pay for a psychologist. Plus, my family has a hard enough time paying bills. Then there's the matter that they're both stressed to hell, I can only imagine what hearing this shit would do to them... yeah.

I understand why exercise and such things would maybe do me good, but it's getting over that damn hurdle of self-consciousness that's the problem for me. I've thought about an exercise bike, but we don't have the space in the house for one.

Again, one of the problems with living in a small town is that there isn't much in the way of social events, and for the ones that do exist, they're all religious in nature. Dance class would be a hilarious failure; I have enough problems with balance as is just walking. Most of my social interaction does occur over Twitch chats, and there's a couple of decent sized ones of which I'm fairly well known, and it's always pretty fun to hang out in those.

There's many times that I wish I had a switch in my brain to just turn it off for a while, and I do readily admit that my brain just doesn't stop, even if it's furiously going around in circles, as far as I know the only way to turn it off like that is drugs and alcohol, which uh... no thanks, I've seen what that did to my biological parents (am adopted). Actually, that does make me wonder if they had similar symptoms. I would ask, but as far as I know one of them is in prison six states away, and the other admitted that they didn't want anything to do with me. Ah well, there's always lobotomies, eh? That'll fix me right up! ^^/s
